Theme

Church life

the Holy Spirit noun

also Holy Spirit, Holy Ghost, the Spirit, the Paraclete, the Comforter

late Latin

Vulg. Mt. 28.19
Aus. Ephem. 2.18 (Lewis & Short)
Cod. Just. 1.1.1 (Lewis & Short)

Spīritus Sānctus, Spīritūs Sānctī m.

The two churches’ Creed differs here: the Latin Church confesses the Spirit quī ex Patre Fīliōque prōcēdit, the Orthodox Church, with the Greek text of 381, as proceeding from the Father (τὸ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρὸς ἐκπορευόμενον).

Other words

  • 1Paraclītus: spelled with ī (Lewis & Short paraclētus). The Clementine Vulgate’s and the Roman Breviary’s spelling (Jo. 14.26), from Greek παράκλητος with η said as ī; the Stuttgart Vulgate prints paraclētus (Latinitas Precēs, Notae).

    Paraclītus1, Paraclītī m. — the Paraclete, the Comforter

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Jo. 14.26 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Greek παράκλητος, the one called to help.

Examples

  • in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī

    in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy SpiritVulg. Mt. 28.19

  • Paraclītus autem Spīritus Sānctus, quem mittet Pater in nōmine meō, ille vōs docēbit omnia

    But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all thingsVulg. Jo. 14.26

See also the Trinity, God, Pentecost, sign.
